newsitem.title: UK: British school closes due to assault on teacher.
newsitem.headline: British school closes due to assault on teacher.

text.p: A British school at the centre of a nationwide debate about public morality was closed on Thursday after a sexual assault by a pupil on a woman teacher.
The Ridings School in Halifax, northern England, was closed after the assault, a spokeswoman for the Calderdale Education Authority, which runs the school, said.
Earlier teachers at the school voted unanimously in favour of strike action because of the threat from unruly pupils.

Nigel de Gruchy, general secretary of the NASUWT teachers union, said serious disturbances began even while government inspectors, sent in by the government to look into the school's problems, were on the premises on Wednesday.
There is no timetable for reopening the school, De Gruchy said.

"I understand this measure is to take effect until further notice, or at least until a new head teacher can be appointed," he said. He added that teachers would go on an indefinite strike if at least 12 pupils were not expelled from the school.
The Ridings School has been in the headlines since teachers threatened to walk out 10 days ago unless dozens of disruptive pupils were either suspended or expelled.
The school has prompted a nationwide debate on the standard of discipline amongst young people, the lack of parental control in modern Britain and a general decline in moral standards.
Some members of the ruling Conservative party have called for the reintroduction of corporal punishment in schools. Use of the cane was banned in British state schools in 1985.
A 16-year-old was imprisoned for life earlier this month after stabbing a London headmaster to death last December as he rushed to protect one of his teenaged pupils from a gang of youths.
